note: Reviewed column references the worker makes that no table provides. An entry here is a live gap with a stated consequence, not an accepted pattern — the gate fails on NEW entries, and also on an entry here that has since been created, so this list cannot go stale. Fixing one means deleting its line. The onboardingChecklist.ts entries are D184's audit: every one is a checklist item that reads 'not done' for every account forever, because num() swallows the error and 0 > 0 is false. Each names the column to repoint to; D184's follow-up PRs empty them.

columns.compliance_records.record_type: checklist ef.83b and ef.ip. The table's column is `type`, and the query already ORs against it — so the OR arm is live and this arm is dead weight. Delete the arm rather than rename it.
columns.compliance_records.user_id: checklist ef.83b and ef.ip. compliance_records is keyed on subsidiary_id / deal_id / created_by and carries no subject column at all, so neither item can ever be satisfied by this table. Needs a decision, not a rename: created_by is the nearest fact and means something different.
columns.corporate_profiles.kyb_status: services/trust.ts resyncKycKyb reads it to decide whether a kyb_v1 legal_obligation is satisfied. The column exists on no table in this schema, so the SELECT throws into its catch, rows is empty, and the whole KYB reconciliation loop is a no-op. NOT given a column, because that alone would not help: nothing anywhere writes a KYB decision. /trust/kyb/start upserts entity_name, registration_number and registered_country and sets the obligation to in_review; there is no provider callback and no admin approve/reject that would ever set a status. Completing the KYB decision path is feature work and a product question — which store, which values, who writes them — not a rename.
columns.expert_bookings.expert_user_id: checklist mt.booking. The column is `expert_id` (a row in experts, not a user id). Repointing also needs the join to experts.user_id, because the checklist has a user id in hand.
columns.expert_bookings.founder_user_id: checklist nf.advisor. The column is `user_id` — the booker. Straight repoint.
columns.experts.comp_model: checklist mt.comp. No such column. pricing_model exists but is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'paid', so repointing to it would flip the item from never-satisfiable to always-satisfiable — gate on hourly_rate_usd or first_session_free instead, which are the facts an advisor actually fills in.
columns.experts.tags: checklist mt.tags. The columns are categories_json and sectors_json. Repoint, and test for a non-empty JSON array rather than a non-empty string.
columns.experts.weekly_capacity: checklist mt.capacity. No such column, and the fact is on a different entity: advisors.weekly_hours_band (migration 182), reached via users.advisor_id. The whole mt.* catalogue joins experts — the wellbeing directory — where it means advisors.
columns.financial_models.user_id: checklist ef.financials. The table is keyed on project_id; repoint through the caller's project, as nf.project and nf.okrs already do.
columns.investor_introductions.introducer_user_i: checklist op.intro. No such column. The table's two party columns are investor_user_id and founder_user_id; a partner who made the introduction is not recorded on it at all, so this needs a decision rather than a rename.
columns.investor_introductions.source_user_id: checklist op.intro, same query, same absence as introducer_user_id above.
columns.investor_profiles.deployment_target_cent: checklist inv.target. No such column. The nearest stored facts are ticket_min_usd, ticket_max_usd and lp_target_usd — none of them a deployment target, and all in dollars rather than cents. A decision, not a rename.
columns.investor_profiles.reserve_percent: checklist inv.target, same query. Nothing on investor_profiles records a reserve policy.
columns.investor_profiles.thesis: checklist inv.thesis. The column is thesis_text. Straight repoint.
columns.match_scores.investor_user_id: checklist inv.review. The columns are user_id and target_user_id. Repointing needs a decision on which side an investor sits — score_type is what distinguishes them.
columns.pairwise_ndas.user_a: checklist ef.nda / inv.nda / mt.nda, the fallback arm. The columns are party_a_user_id and party_b_user_id. The arm above it (esign_envelopes) is live, so the item is satisfiable today — but only through e-sign, never through an existing pairwise NDA.
columns.pairwise_ndas.user_b: same query and same absence as user_a above; the column is party_b_user_id.
columns.partner_deals.founder_user_id: the trust-score partner-deal signal (services/newsTrust.ts:70). safeFirst degrades to null, so partner_deal_signed never awards its 10 points to anyone. The column is user_id. One of three dead signals in that function — see partners.owner_user_id and the spinout_lab_state table entry; 35 points of trust score that can never be earned.
columns.partner_deals.partner_user_id: checklist op.deal_type. The column is user_id. Its sibling in the same query, signed_at, is also absent.
columns.partner_deals.signed_at: checklist op.deal_type. The nearest column is activated_at; partner_invitations carries the signed_at that this query is probably reaching for.
columns.partner_profiles.conflicts_disclosed_at: checklist op.conflicts. No such column. conflicts_text exists and holds the disclosure itself, so a non-empty conflicts_text is the honest test — there is no timestamp to record when it was made.
columns.partners.owner_user_id: the trust-score KYB signal (services/newsTrust.ts:62). safeFirst degrades to null, so kyb_verified never awards its 15 points. partners is an email-keyed directory with no user foreign key at all — it cannot be joined to a user id, so this is a decision rather than a rename. partner_profiles.user_id is the table that does link the two.
columns.references_records.user_id: checklist op.refs and mt.refs. THE COLUMN IS NOT THE PROBLEM — the table is. migrations/034_unmounted_routes.sql declares references_records with a subject_user_id column, but schema_baseline.sql does not carry it and production does not have it (read read-only against studioos-db, 2026-09-21). So a freshly provisioned database and HQ's own are both missing it, and both items are broken by an absent table rather than a renamed column. Repointing to subject_user_id would fix nothing. That migration 034 declares a table neither the baseline nor production has is baseline drift and belongs to check-baseline-drift, filed separately.
columns.referral_invites.owner_user_id: checklist op.referral. The column is sender_user_id. Straight repoint.
